# Why do we have slides in a talk? {background-color="var(--divider-bg)"}

::: {.notes}
A good place to start is being clear on why we have slides in a talk in the first place…
:::

## {.center background-image="images/pic_basketball_goal.jpg" background-size="auto 100%" background-position="right center"}

::: {.text-panel-left-60}
::: {.slide-body-heading}
The [goal]{.emphasis} of any talk is [audience impact]{.emphasis}.
:::
:::

##  {.center background-image="images/pic_basketball_goal.jpg" background-size="auto 100%" background-position="right center"}

::: {.text-panel-left-60}
::: {.slide-body-heading}
[Slides]{.emphasis} don't drive impact.
:::
::: {.fragment .slide-body-heading}
[The talk]{.emphasis} drives impact.
:::
::: {.fragment .slide-body-heading}
Slides simply [reinforce the talk]{.emphasis}.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Slides are not where a talk starts.

Don't worry! We WILL talk about slides. We just want to be clear that
slides are not where a talk starts.
:::

## {.center background-image="images/pic_boulder_support.jpg" background-size="auto 100%" background-position="right center"}

::: {.text-panel-left-60}
::: {.slide-body-heading}
So what does [reinforcement]{.emphasis} actually [mean]{.emphasis}?
:::
:::
::: {.notes}
Image source: https://unsplash.com/photos/man-standing-beside-rock-formation-mj51pZwan9c
:::

## {.center background-image="images/pic_boulder_support.jpg" background-size="auto 100%" background-position="right center"}

::: {.text-panel-left-60}
::: {.slide-body-heading}
Hold their [attention]{.emphasis}.
:::
::: {.slide-body-heading .fragment}
Help them [understand]{.emphasis} what's being presented.
:::
::: {.slide-body-heading .fragment}
Enable them to [retain]{.emphasis} what matters most.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
- **Keep the audience's attention** — the talk is bound by time and attention
- **Understand and care about the information** — by directly reinforcing what the speaker is saying
- **Remember it** — dual-encoding with multiple senses (hearing *and* seeing); brain science backs up that using multiple senses aids retention

What slides should not (primarily) do: remind the speaker what they're supposed to be  (although they *can* be a visual aid to keep the speaker on track; that's just a natural artifact if they do their primary job well!)

Image source: https://unsplash.com/photos/man-standing-beside-rock-formation-mj51pZwan9c
:::
